residuals.by_project_unattributed_note: The eight named projects account for 397,300 of 408,364 lines. The remaining 11,064 sit in projects the brief does not break out individually (the smaller side projects and tools). Label any leftover slice "everything else", never zero it.
residuals.by_language_unattributed_note: The six named languages account for 407,000 lines; the remaining 1,364 are other languages the brief does not list.

conflicts_with_other_measurements.subject: Browser
conflicts_with_other_measurements.other_measurement_says: 63,029 JavaScript lines + 13,218 CSS lines = 76,247 (CONTENT-UPDATE.md §1, `git ls-files | xargs wc -l`)
conflicts_with_other_measurements.why: Different rules. The census counts CODE lines; `wc -l` counts every line including blanks and comments, and `git ls-files` sweeps a different file set. Neither figure is wrong; they are not interchangeable. Do not add them together or present them side by side without saying which rule each used.

conflicts_with_other_measurements.subject: TVHA portal
conflicts_with_other_measurements.why: Same reason as above: code lines vs. raw line count over a different file set.

conflicts_with_other_measurements.subject: Atlas
conflicts_with_other_measurements.other_measurement_says: ~140k app lines and ~212k test lines (the figures on the baseline write-up, listed there as NOT remeasured)
conflicts_with_other_measurements.why: The two were measured with different rules and do not reconcile: 140k + 212k = 352k against the census’s 228.5k. The census is the 16 Sep measurement and is the one to publish. The ~140k/~212k pair is explicitly flagged unverified in CONTENT-UPDATE.md and should not be shown beside the census figure.
